claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Solutionizing produces a homogenized microstructure with minimal segregation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local chemical fluctuations and short-range order in equimolar HfNbTaTiZr alter dislocation activity as temperature changes.
Changes in dislocation activity caused by local chemical order explain the alloy's elevated-temperature stress-strain response.
Changes in dislocation activity or chemical order explain the alloy's elevated-temperature thermal-expansion behavior.
Changes in dislocation activity or chemical order explain the alloy's elevated-temperature elastic moduli.
Short-range order or local chemical heterogeneity modifies dislocation pathways and lattice parameters at elevated temperatures.
Above approximately 800 °C, short-range order emerges or grows in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order alters the effective energy barriers for dislocation slip.
The ordering-induced change in slip barriers produces a moderated increase in dislocation interactions.
The proposed ordering mechanism concurrently changes thermal expansion and stiffness.
Relative to an RHEA lacking strong short-range order, HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit plateauing or reduced temperature dependence of flow stress above approximately 800 °C.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit anomalies in its coefficient of thermal expansion above approximately 800 °C.
High-temperature loading will produce XRD peak shifts or broadening indicative of local chemical ordering.
An RHEA lacking significant short-range order should show more typical thermal softening.
An RHEA lacking significant short-range order should show a linear increase in thermal expansion with temperature.
Above approximately 1200 °C, phase transformations or partial melting may dominate and invalidate the short-range-order mechanism.
Short-range ordering has been observed in some high-entropy alloys, but its presence and high-temperature effect in HfNbTaTiZr remain unclear because direct in situ data are limited.
